programme.title: Football: 2026 World Cup – quarter-final match: Spain – Belgium
programme.desc: The European champions reached the quarter-finals of the World Cup without conceding a single goal along the way. Much of this is due to Unai Simon, who became the longest undefeated goalkeeper in the history of the World Cup. In the round of 16 match, Lamine Yamal and company ended not only Portugal's adventure in the World Cup, but also Cristiano Ronaldo's World Cup history. The Spaniards will face the Belgians. After reversing the fate of the match against Senegal (3-2) in the round of 16, the Red Devils gained momentum and defeated the co-hosts of the world championship, the Americans, 4-1 in the previous round. Will they find a way to dismantle La Furia Roja's iron defense in the quarterfinals? Their task will be made more difficult by the absence of Amadou Onana, who suffered a serious injury in the previous match

programme.title: Football: 2026 World Cup – quarter-final match: Norway – England
programme.desc: The Norwegians have already deserved to be called the dark horse of the American World Cup. In the knockout phase, they first eliminated Senegal from the tournament (2:1), and then made a surprise by eliminating Brazil (2:1) with Vinicius Junior at the helm. Now the English are standing in the way of the Stale Solbakken team, having had difficult experiences in both the round of 16 (DR Congo 2:1) and the round of 16 (Mexico 3:2). The highlight of the match at Miami Stadium should be a duel between super snipers - Erling Haaland and Harry Kane. The former has already scored seven goals during the World Cup, the latter has six goals

programme.title: Football: World Cup 2026 – quarter-final match: Argentina – Switzerland
programme.desc: Argentina has already received two serious warnings in the knockout phase. In the 1/16 finals, the Cape Verdean players were surprised twice, which sensationally led to overtime against the defending champions. However, in the 1/8 finals, Leo Messi and his teammates were out of the World Cup until the 83rd minute. Against Egypt, they had a brilliant end to the match, scoring three goals. They will face Switzerland in the match to advance to the top four. The Helvetii defeated the Colombian team in the 1/8 finals only after a penalty shootout

programme.desc: The series presents the profiles of people working behind the scenes of Polish football clubs. They perform very important duties necessary for the functioning of the team, which are often invisible to outsiders. Krzysztof Kozik has been the manager of the first team of Bruk-Bet Termalica Nieciecza for 20 years. He has been a resident of Nieciecza since birth. In the 1980s, he reactivated the LZS Nieciecza football club, which is an Ekstraklasa newcomer in the 2025/26 season. programme.desc: The series directed by Maciej Klimek presents five PKO BP Ekstraklasa players who took responsibility for their teams at the decisive moments of the 2025/26 season. The heroes are Jesus Imaz (Jagiellonia Białystok), Rifet Kapić (Lechia Gdańsk), Radosław Murawski (Lech Poznań), Julian Shehu (Widzew Łódź) and Karol Czubak (Motor Lublin). Cameras follow them on and off the pitch, showing the pressure, behind-the-scenes of matches and their private lives. The story of Radosław Murawski, one of the key players of Lech Poznań, who struggled with a serious, months-long injury. The camera accompanies him during this difficult period. The player is fighting to return to the pitch, not knowing whether he will play at the highest level again. It is a story about determination, mental strength and support from loved ones, as well as the hope that he will be able to help the team defend the championship title. Poland. 2026. documentary series

programme.title: David Attenborough: songs of life
programme.desc: Sir David Attenborough selects seven of the most extraordinary recordings from the natural world and explores what these sounds mean to specific animal species. Each song - from that of a lemur, through the song of a humpback whale or a lyrebird from the order of passerine birds - was recorded during the lifetime of a famous naturalist who recorded and analyzed these songs for decades. The oldest recording was made when Sir David was five years old, the latest just a few years before the documentary was created. Each has an amazing story behind it and shows how much we still don't know about the natural world. When Sir David Attenborough was born, the science of song was transformed under Charles Darwin's theory of sexual selection, which labeled singing dangerous because it revealed the singer's location to predators. The same song also gives males a great chance to be noticed by the female and thus to pass on their genes to the next generation of birds. So the males sing, and the females listen and choose the best singers because, according to them, they will be the best fathers. New scientific trends in bird song are challenging these long-held ideas. Scientists invited to the program show that in fact, in most species of songbirds, females create their own songs - and only now do they have a chance to be truly heard. However, there is a concern whether we will be able to learn all the songs of these extraordinary birds - the human loss is loud, and the planet Earth is falling silently, as the host of the program also warns. The production is a continuation of the documentary film nominated for the Grierson Award. Great Britain. 2022. documentary film

programme.title: 30 for 30: Boo-Yah: A Portrait of Stuart Scott
programme.desc: 30 for 30 (Sports). As part of its 30th anniversary celebration, ESPN looks back at notable sports happenings that occurred from 1979 to 2009 with this documentary series featuring 30 films from some of Hollywood's finest directors and producers. Peter Berg, Barry Levinson, John Singleton, Spike Jonze, Dan Klores, Barbara Kopple, Ron Shelton and Albert Maysles are among the filmmakers involved, and the stories told include the shocking trade of Wayne Gretzky in 1988, the Baltimore Colts' nighttime move in 1984, Reggie Miller's rivalry with the New York Knicks, the death of Len Bias in 1986, a profile of George Steinbrenner and his family business, and a look at Michael Jordan's attempt at a baseball career. A new series of 30 films premiered in October 2012 with «Broke,» about the challenges athletes face in managing their money

programme.title: Secret Life of the Wombat: Wombat Wood (S1E1). Dokumentika, apie gamtą. JAV, 2016. S1, Ep1
programme.desc: 2016 г. Год: 2016. Страна: JAV. Год: 2016. S1 «Secret Life Of the Wombat»…In the cool highlands near Australia's Snowy Mountains is Wombat Wood. There, dotted amongst the trees and dense foliage, are over a hundred wombat burrows. But when some of the burrows are flooded, the wombats need to find safetyThe island continent of Australia is home to some of the most unique and fascinating flora and fauna on the planet. While some of the more iconic animals, such as the kangaroo and the koala, are fairly well known, other creatures can prove to be just as captivating. One of these is the wombat, a beast with peculiar burrowing habits, convoluted mating rituals and cube-shaped droppings. Found mostly in the forests of the southeastern corner of the mainland and on Tasmania, wombats tend to sleep during the day and emerge from their burrows at night in search for food. Enjoying a mostly solitary existence, wombats do partake in social niceties when it comes to mating season which involves an energetic chase for female companionshipDirector: Ashley DaviesCast: Virge Gilchrist

programme.title: Animal Empires: Animals Gone Wild (S1E3). Documentary about nature. USA, 2016. S1, Ep3
programme.desc: 2016 г. Год: 2016. Страна: JAV. Год: 2016. S1, Ep3 «Animal Empire»…As the popular characters of songs and stories, farm animals are celebrated all over the world. But few stories tell of their sister species who live in the wild. These animals known primarily as livestock, beasts of burden, or even pets must fend for themselves beyond the fences of their domesticated kinAnimals congregate in places where their basic needs can be met: havens from predators where competition for food is manageable and breeding opportunities are abundant. Journey to the habitats of these one-of-a-kind animals and learn their survival stories, from nesting fairy penguins, to migrating caribouDirector: Scott Simpson, John Wesley Chisholm

programme.title: Land of Primates: Lemurs of Anja Mountain (S1E1). Dokumentika, apie gamtą. JAV, 2016. S1, Ep1
programme.desc: 2016 г. Год: 2016. Страна: JAV. Год: 2016. S1, Ep1 «Land of Primates»…Millions of years ago, castaway creatures found themselves stranded on Madagascar's rugged shores. Isolated from the mainland, the newcomers were left to evolve. This is a magical world of rare and unique creatures perfectly adapted to their tropical hideawayThis fascinating documentary series takes a close look at some of our closest relatives in the animal kingdom: the primates. Explore the characteristics, lifestyles and personalities of these resilient creatures as they face daily challenges in their quest for survival. The film crew visist Madagascar, home to several species of lemur, some found nowhere else on the planet, and we examine how they have adapted to the habitat of this unique island. In the heart of South Africa, an alpha male baboon has to protect his family from a dangerous rival gang. The Semien region of Ethiopia is home to geladas, mountain primates who overcome the difficulties of their rocky home. In Zanzibar, the colobus monkey face the threat of being hunted to extinctionDirector: Claudio Velazques-Rojas, Jordan-Laine Calder

programme.desc: The depths of the ocean, inaccessible to human gaze, never cease to attract the attention of researchers. Aquatic life, stretching over billions of cubic kilometers, is fraught with a great variety of amazing and strange inhabitants: from giant to miniature, from bright to inconspicuous, from harmless to poisonous, from prey to hunters. Spain

programme.title: d/f The Mystery of the Life of Seals
programme.desc: The film shows breathtaking footage of the underwater world of gray seals in the Stockholm archipelago. Viewers will learn how these mammals learn to hunt, swim and survive in the harsh conditions of the icy waters of the Baltic Sea. The film also talks about why, despite accusations from fishermen of depleting fish stocks, seals play a crucial role in maintaining the balance of the Baltic ecosystem. Sweden

programme.title: d/f Is it about love?
programme.desc: The filmmakers delve into the behavior of animals, trying to find out if it is possible for them to feel the same emotions that we do. Particular attention is paid to the mating season of males and the relationship of females with offspring. This research sheds light on whether animals can experience feelings such as love and how their emotions are similar to humans. Dir.: Juan Antonio Rodriguez Llano, Juan Luis Santos. Spain

programme.title: d/s African stories of the cheetah family. 1 p.
programme.desc: Maleika is a cheetah from the Maasai Mara reserve. Her life is like a roller coaster and they made a movie about her. Maleika’s motto is “Never give up!” She can purr, hiss and chirp. Maleika loves freedom, because her habitat is open and spacious. Spain

programme.title: d/s African stories of the cheetah family. 5 s.
programme.desc: And in East Africa, Matto Barfuss in 2013, north of the Serengeti, came across a cheetah - Maleika. Matto was convinced that she was Diana's great-granddaughter. He decided to share the story of this incredible cheetah with the world. Spain

programme.title: d/f Legend of the Malabar bird-rhinoceros
programme.desc: In the forests of southern China, the rare crowned kalao is forced to seek increasingly unusual nesting sites, from cavities high in the canopy to limestone caves. Scientists from China and Thailand have been observing the birds for years, studying their habits and helping to preserve the species through artificial nests and habitat restoration. China

programme.title: d/s Animal Superpowers (Superhuman Senses)
programme.desc: A series that explores the amazing senses of animals and their evolution. Why do snakes have forked tongues and elephants have huge ears? How do bats and moths use their unusual ears and antennae for orientation? In each episode, we explore how these features, which at first glance seem strange, play a key role in survival. Like humans, animals rely on their senses to find food, communicate, and avoid danger. An in-depth look at how evolution has created unique tools to adapt to our environment. This exciting journey will reveal the secrets of the hunters at the top of the food chain. Dir.: Paul Dean. USA

programme.desc: Everyone knows the name of the famous Portuguese football player Cristiano Ronaldo, but few can imagine his life before he became famous. At the age of 8, the boy began playing for an amateur football team, thanks to the fact that his father worked there. After Ronaldo was noticed by coaches of famous football clubs, his career took off rapidly. Now he signs contracts with large fees and no longer remembers poverty. Dir.: Anthony Vonk. Starring: Dolores Aveiro, Hugo Aveiro, Georgie Bingham, Adrian Clarke, Rio Ferdinand, Claudia Garcia, David Alvarez Izquierdo, Rhiannon Jones, Nelvino Lima, Miguel Lopez Marquez. Great Britain, 2015, biography, documentary, sports

programme.title: d/f Maradona. Best ever

Interviews with loved ones, partners and experts will help reveal the secrets of Maradona’s greatness, his unique talent and difficult fate.

programme.title: Wild Japan – land of a thousand islands
programme.desc:
Japan, with its four main islands and over 6,000 mostly uninhabited islets, stretches over 3,000 kilometers from the Sea of ​​Okhotsk to the Philippine Sea. Flora and fauna fascinate. 

On Honshu, the largest island, there is both urban areas and wilderness. At the temple complex, with the world's largest bronze Buddha statue, in the former capital Nara, wild sika deer are the attraction. The Japanese worship them as messengers of the gods. In addition, every year the impressive cherry tree blossoms in spring attract tourists from all over the world.

Macaques are also increasingly venturing out of the hinterland to find more convenient sources of food. For example, the curious monkeys bathe in hot thermal springs. The spectacle attracts many tourists, who in turn throw small treats into the water for the macaques. Only when the monkeys are full do they retreat into the wild in the evening.

programme.title: Wild Japan – land of a thousand islands
programme.desc: The south of Japan is brimming with harsh natural forces, ocean, volcanoes, typhoons. The remote islands offer a paradise for animals. Incredible symbioses of monkeys and deer can be found here. (Station info).

programme.title: Wild Japan – land of a thousand islands
programme.desc: From arctic cold to midsummer: the living conditions on Hokkaido are a challenge for animals. Nevertheless, many species such as the brown bear live on Japan's northernmost island. (Station info).

programme.title: Wild Scandinavia
programme.desc: The natural coast of Scandinavia is home to orcas, otters and sea eagles. Only the most resilient survive here in the merciless weather conditions. (Station info).

programme.title: Wild Scandinavia
programme.desc: Wolves, lynxes and reindeer feel at home here: in the magical forests surrounded by waterways in the heart of Scandinavia. As the seasons progress, they form surprising alliances. (Station info).

programme.title: Wild Scandinavia
programme.desc: How do musk oxen, polar bears and arctic foxes cope with the endlessly long polar nights in Scandinavia? And how do they adapt to changing environmental conditions? (Station info).

programme.title: Wild Brazil
programme.desc: Capuchin monkeys, giant otters and coatis raise their offspring in Brazil's wilderness. Extreme landscapes, changeable weather and deadly hunters characterize her early life. (Station info).

programme.title: Terra X
programme.desc: There are around three million shipwrecks sunk in waters worldwide. They are often the target of looters hoping to make valuable discoveries. They also succumb to decay over time. (Station info).

programme.title: Kieling's Wild World
programme.desc: Researchers are certain: We are currently experiencing the worst species extinction since the end of the dinosaurs. Animal filmmaker Andreas Kieling explores threatened habitats on three continents and speaks to researchers and animal rights activists. \n\nThe island of Madagascar, where Kieling observes ring-tailed lemurs, is almost a continent in itself. The jungle home of this lemur species is threatened by deforestation. In Alaska's Denali National Park, climate change is causing problems for many species - including the last 49 wolves that live and hunt there.

programme.title: Kieling's Wild World
programme.desc: 15,000 orangutans live in Sumatra today: - sixty percent fewer than in 1985. Kieling visits the Bukit Tigapuluh National Park, where orphaned great apes are made fit for the wild. In Iceland he tags young puffins with ornithologists.

programme.title: Amazonia – Expedition into the rainforest

programme.title: The great parks in Africa

programme.title: The great elephant story

programme.title: Africa's Wild Sides
programme.desc: There is finally hope for the animals of Mashatu, it is raining. However, this is stronger than it has been for years. The abundance of water brings new life, a blessing after four years of drought. (Station info).

programme.title: Africa: jaws and claws
programme.desc: One of the oldest predators on earth lives along South Africa's coast: the shark. After 400 million years of evolution, the fascinating hunters of the sea are now threatened with extinction. (Station info).

programme.title: Africa: jaws and claws
programme.desc: Lizards and snakes have conquered almost every habitat in Africa. The reptiles mostly operate in secret, thanks to a number of remarkable survival techniques. (Station info).

programme.title: The World of Sharks – Amazing Findings
programme.desc: Sharks as perfect hunters: from pack hunting of blacktip sharks to lurking carpet sharks. The highlight is the great white shark seal hunt in spectacular images. (Station info).

programme.title: Crazy but true!
programme.desc: Regardless of whether you encounter a cute-looking monkey or a potentially poisonous spider, there is one lesson we humans should internalize when it comes to wild animals: keep your distance! (Station info).

programme.title: Crazy but true!

programme.title: SOUR, SALTY & ALIVE
